newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-BICHETTE STAYS HOT AS ROCKIES BEAT CUBS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-BICHETTE STAYS HOT AS ROCKIES BEAT CUBS.

text.p: Dante Bichette stayed red-hot with a two-run homer and four RBI as the Colorado Rockies beat the Chicago Cubs 6-3 for their fourth straight win Saturday.

Bichette had a two-run single in the first and his homer, a 455-foot (139 metres) blast to left in the sixth off Terry Mulholland (6-10), gave the Rockies a 6-1 lead. Bichette has 13 RBI in the first three games of the four-game set.

"It's been a good week," Bichette said. "If I could explain it, I'd like to thank the fans. With all the trade rumours, they realised that I might be traded. One guy had this sign as big as two lockers that said, 'Dante must stay.' That has really been exciting. I'm in a hot streak and I'll ride it as long as I can."
Roger Bailey (9-7) allowed three runs and eight hits with two walks and a strikeout over eight innings. Darren Holmes worked the ninth for his third save.
Mulholland was hammered for six runs and seven hits over 5 1/3 innings with three walks and one strikeout. The left-hander has won just once in his last 10 starts.
Shawon Dunston accounted for the Chicago offence with a solo homer and two-run single.

Colorado's Larry Walker went 0-for-3 with a run scored and saw his average fall to .390, the lowest since he was hitting .375 on April 4, the fourth game of the season. In his last 11 games, Walker is just 8-for-38 (.211), lowering his average 21 points.
In San Diego, Sterling Hitchcock allowed one run over six strong innings and Chris Gomez added a key two-run single as the Padres beat the New York Mets 5-3.

Hitchcock (7-5) allowed a double and four singles, walking three and striking out six. He threw 60 of 101 pitches for strikes and held New York to just two hits through four innings as San Diego built a 3-0 lead.
Bobby Jones (12-6) took the loss.
The Padres have won six of their last seven games, 12 of 15 and are 13-4 since the All-Star break. They have gained seven games on first-place San Francisco since the break.
San Diego's Tony Gwynn went 2-for-4 to raise his batting average to .391.

In Los Angeles, Mike Piazza hit a pair of homers and drove in three runs and Darren Dreifort pitched a career-high 4 1/3 innings in relief of an injured Hideo Nomo as the Dodgers defeated the Philadelphia Phillies 4-1.
Piazza hit a solo shot in the first inning and added a two-run blast, his 22nd, in the sixth for the Dodgers.

Dreifort (4-1) came on with two outs in the fourth inning after Nomo was struck on his pitching elbow by a ball hit by Scott Rolen. Nomo left with a contusion on his right elbow and will be re-evaluated Sunday.

The Phillies, who dropped to 1-4 on their eight-game road trip, wasted a strong performance by Curt Schilling (11-10), who struck out 10 and walked none but gave up four runs and seven hits over seven innings.
In Cincinnati, Pokey Reese singled home Deion Sanders with the winning run in the 11th and the Reds hit three homers, two by Eduardo Perez in a 7-6 victory over the Atlanta Braves.
Bret Boone also homered although Atlanta manager Bobby Cox got ejected for arguing that it had been a foul ball.
The Reds won for the first time under interim manager Jack McKeon, who replaced the fired Ray Knight on Friday and lost to the Braves in the opener of the three-game series.
Cincinnati won for just the second time in eight games and defeated the Braves for the first time in seven meetings this season.
Javy Lopez homered twice for Atlanta.

In Houston, Sean Berry's leadoff homer in the bottom of the 10th off Ugueth Urbina (3-7), after J.R. Phillips's pinch-hit homer in the ninth tied the game, lifted the Astros to their season-high eighth straight win, 9-8 over the Montreal Expos.
Rondell White homered twice and drove in four runs for the Expos, who lost their fourth straight.

In San Francisco, Tony Womack snapped a sixth-inning tie with an RBI single and Kevin Young and Dale Sveum drove in two runs each in the six-run frame, helping the Pittsburgh Pirates to a 10-3 victory over the Giants.
Kevin Polcovich had three hits -- a single, double and triple -- and scored three runs for the Pirates, who have won 10 of their last 11 contests at 3Com Park.
In St. Louis, Delino DeShields hit a two-run pinch homer in the seventh to snap a tie and Matt Morris allowed one run over 7 2/3 innings as the Cardinals dumped the Florida Marlins 3-1.
Royce Clayton accounted for the Cards' other run with a solo homer in the first. St. Louis snapped a three-game losing streak.
